archetypes.name: generator-output-fidelity
archetypes.rationale: The plan claims rule #9 lands verbatim in both implementer artifacts via deterministic generators; verify the generator sed targets do not inadvertently transform any substring of the new rule text.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read scripts/generate-codex-implementer.sh and scripts/generate-cursor-implementer.sh to enumerate every sed substitution target and confirm none collides with text in the proposed Hard guard #9 (keywords: exec_command, write_stdin, read_stdout, status=bailed, bail_reason, persistent interactive subprocess sessions). Verify scripts/generators.tsv lists both generators by name and that scripts/check-generators.sh implements a --check mode that exits non-zero on drift. Confirm agents/codex-implementer.md and agents/cursor-implementer.md currently carry an AUTO-GENERATED marker and that make lint invokes check-generators.sh transitively. If any generator sed pattern overlaps rule #9 text, the verbatim-landing claim in the plan is false and the implementer would produce a silently corrupted artifact without a lint signal. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: harness-phrase-alignment
archetypes.rationale: The plan uses slightly different grep phrase variants across the two test harnesses; verify the exact strings match clause text and that insertion points in existing assertion blocks exist at the described line numbers.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read skills/implement/scripts/test-codex-implementer.sh and scripts/test-launch-codex-ci.sh to verify the current grep assertion block structure at the line ranges cited in the plan (lines 25-26 and lines 41-46 respectively). Check whether the plan's proposed grep target "persistent interactive subprocess sessions" (with "sessions") in test-codex-implementer.sh and "persistent interactive subprocess" (without "sessions") in test-launch-codex-ci.sh are both guaranteed to match the final clause text in their respective source files, since a substring mismatch silently produces a false-passing assertion. Confirm that grep -Fq versus grep -q usage in each file is consistent with the existing assertion style, as style drift can cause subtly different match semantics and break the consolidated if-block structure the plan requires. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: sibling-md-placement
archetypes.rationale: The plan conditionally targets named sections in sibling .md files that may not exist under those names; verify actual section headers before the implementation attempts a conditional insertion.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read scripts/launch-codex-ci.md, skills/implement/scripts/test-codex-implementer.md, and scripts/test-launch-codex-ci.md to determine whether the sections the plan targets for one-line bullet additions ("Prompt construction" or "Inputs", "Coverage" or "Assertions") actually exist and match the expected heading level. Evaluate whether the conditional branch in the plan for launch-codex-ci.md ("if no such section exists, add ## Subprocess tool discipline") is the branch that will execute, since an incorrect branch choice produces either a misplaced bullet or a spurious new section alongside an existing one. Also confirm that each sibling .md file's existing structure can accept an appended single bullet without disrupting numbered lists, ordered assertions, or structured content that would shift line references relied on by other tests. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
